faq.a: Asiyah is associated with the Arabic form آسية, whose core sense is asiya (wife of pharaoh).

faq.q: What is the origin of Asiyah?
faq.a: Asiyah is associated with Arabic. Variant romanization of آسية. The source record's gloss 'Companion of the Prophet' is unsupported.
Yes — the underlying form آسية is Arabic.
Asiyah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Asiyah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. آسية is the wife of Pharaoh referred to in Qur'an 66:11 and 28:9

faq.q: What does Asiyah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Asiyah is rendered آسیہ and carries the sense آسیہ (فرعون کی بیوی).

faq.q: What does Asiyah mean in Persian?
faq.a: No verified Persian form was established for Asiyah.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-siyah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Asiyah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Asiyah, asiyah. Script forms are آسية, آسیه, آسیہ, आसिया.

faq.q: Is Asiyah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
